gen-gf-oxanium-gf-stack-sans-headline: Big, squared-off swagger with a lowercase that towers. Stack Sans Headline holds the quieter job, keeping its wide gaps crisp at tiny sizes, while Oxanium makes the loud entrance.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sono: Sono sets tall lowercase with generous spacing and an a left ajar, wide and friendly across the line. Mystery Quest adds a bookish, nostalgic flourish above it.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-stack-sans-text: Press Start 2P is pure retro fun. Its lightly varied strokes and widely pinned letters earn their keep when set big and brief, while Stack Sans Text draws a flat, marker-like line beneath.
gen-righteous-gf-stack-sans-notch: Righteous bends thin steel rod into bowls that fill the whole line. Stack Sans Notch brings the sturdiest quality of the pair: open curves you can see straight into, drawn like rod stock.
gen-tourney-gf-sulphur-point: Sulphur Point reads with distinct gaps in its letters and a marker-like line, bulky in the lowercase. Tourney, stretched wide and athletic above it, feels like a shouted headline beside a steady voice.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-savate: Savate reads contemporary and clean, with a tall rounded o that nearly matches its capital. Then give it the size adjustments, since its sturdy hairlines and open curves repay a little extra room.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-ruda: Distinctive and bold, Gugi's tall lowercase nearly reaches its capitals. Ruda does the quieter work, a wire-like monoline with a sizable x-height that keeps screen reading comfortable.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-readex-pro: Chunky, upbeat, and held wide open. And Readex Pro carries a longer passage with broad terminal gaps and an unvarying weight, so the text keeps moving without a snag.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Eater's wide letter gaps and short ascenders give it a dark, aggressive bite with moderately weighty stems. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa does the calmer job, its open curves and low stroke variation keeping text clean and modern.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Whimsical, stubby, and a bit bossy. Noto Sans Tagalog lets generous curve gaps and a dominant middle zone settle the line, so Flavors' wire-like monoline towers above something quieter.
